_meta.note: Golden corpus for the ADR 0025 Stage-B thesis-coherence merge adjudicator. GATES 0025-C3: the built adjudicator must pass this corpus (hard cases at 100%, others >=85%) BEFORE its live flip. Pairs 1-8 are REAL verdicts from the 7/11 live replay (scripts/probes/_274_merge_replay.py, operator-visible run) - the replay's driver-based reasoning is the golden. Pairs 9-14 are adversarial synthetics targeting the failure modes a sector-label merger would make. Verdicts: MERGE (one driver, one trade) / DISTINCT (different drivers) / PARENT_CHILD (narrower slice of the same driver). hard=true pairs are zero-tolerance.

theme_a.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
theme_a.description: Multi-line P&C underwriters benefiting from the hard-market pricing cycle: sustained premium-rate increases and underwriting-margin expansion across commercial and personal lines.

theme_b.name: Specialty Catastrophe Property Insurance Underwriters
theme_b.description: Cat-exposed specialty property underwriters whose results are driven by catastrophe-loss experience and reinsurance-linked pricing, re-rating on a benign cat season.

pairs.rationale: The ADR legit-kill anchor: cat-loss experience is a distinct driver-slice within the broad P&C pricing cycle. NEVER a MERGE - collapsing these was the exact failure the exemplars exist to prevent. The replay adjudicated PARENT_CHILD; DISTINCT is also acceptable; MERGE is the tested failure.

theme_a.name: Office REIT Recovery & Re-Rating
theme_a.description: Office REITs re-rating on return-to-office momentum, improving leasing spreads, and distressed-valuation recovery.

theme_b.name: Multifamily Apartment REITs
theme_b.description: Apartment REITs supported by housing-shortage rental demand and defensive cash-flow rotation.

pairs.rationale: The second legit-kill anchor: same sector label (REIT), OPPOSITE drivers (office recovery vs housing-shortage rental demand). Any MERGE here is a sector-label merge - the prohibited move.

theme_a.name: Coastal & Suburban Residential Rental REITs
theme_a.description: Residential rental REITs (coastal and suburban) benefiting from housing-shortage rental demand and institutional rotation into stable residential cash flows.

theme_b.name: Multifamily Apartment REITs
theme_b.description: Apartment REITs supported by sector-wide multifamily investor appetite and defensive rotation into residential stability.

pairs.rationale: The replay's cleanest real merge: BOTH are the housing-rental demand trade - same driver, overlapping holdings, two names for one thesis. (Contrast with M02: the driver, not the REIT label, decides.)

theme_a.name: Pure-Play Quantum Computing Hardware
theme_a.description: Speculative pure-play quantum hardware names driven by the renewed quantum investment cycle and policy support.

theme_b.name: Quantum Computing Hardware & Annealing Systems
theme_b.description: Quantum hardware makers including annealing-approach systems, moving on U.S. quantum funding programs and the same investment cycle.

pairs.rationale: Same macro driver (quantum funding/investment cycle), same asset class, near-identical membership: the annealing qualifier is a technology footnote, not a distinct thesis.

theme_a.name: Clinical-Stage Oncology Drug Development
theme_a.description: Clinical-stage oncology names re-rating on institutional rotation into the space across modalities (ADCs, precision targeting, immuno-oncology).

theme_b.name: Oncology Targeted Therapy Biotechs
theme_b.description: Precision-oncology biotechs benefiting from the same capital rotation into clinical-stage oncology drug developers.

pairs.rationale: One driver (clinical-oncology capital rotation) wearing two names; 'targeted therapy' does not carve a separate demand driver out of the same rotation.

theme_a.name: Quantum Computing & Quantum-Safe Networking
theme_a.description: Quantum-safe cryptography and networking infrastructure names driven by post-quantum security spending.

theme_b.name: Pure-Play Quantum Computing Hardware
theme_b.description: Speculative quantum hardware names driven by the quantum investment cycle and media attention.

pairs.rationale: Shared word ('quantum'), different end-markets: security-infrastructure spending vs hardware speculation. The replay kept them separate; a keyword merger would not.

theme_a.name: Life Insurance & Annuity Providers
theme_a.description: Life and annuity insurers whose earnings are driven by interest rates and investment-portfolio valuations.

theme_b.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Underwriters
theme_b.description: P&C underwriters in the hard-market pricing cycle with expanding underwriting margins.

pairs.rationale: Both 'insurance', unrelated economics: rate-sensitive portfolio earnings vs underwriting-cycle pricing power. The 8-theme insurance family stayed correctly un-merged in the live replay.

theme_a.name: Semiconductor Wafer Foundry & Advanced IC Manufacturing
theme_a.description: Foundries and advanced IC manufacturers driven by the AI-driven wafer-fab capex and utilization cycle.

theme_b.name: Custom AI Silicon & Chip Architecture Licensing
theme_b.description: Chip-architecture and custom-silicon IP licensors monetizing hyperscaler custom-chip design programs.

pairs.rationale: Same sector, different supply-chain position and driver: fab capex/utilization vs design-IP licensing. Semiconductor label alone must not merge the value chain.

theme_a.name: AI Data Center Power Infrastructure
theme_a.description: Power-generation, grid-interconnect, and cooling names re-rating on hyperscaler datacenter electricity demand.

theme_b.name: AI Memory & Storage
theme_b.description: Memory and storage suppliers benefiting from AI-server content growth (HBM, high-capacity NAND).

pairs.rationale: The keyword trap at maximum strength: both are 'AI datacenter' stories, but electricity-demand beneficiaries and memory-content beneficiaries are different industries with different customers and cycles. 'AI' as a stem must never be sufficient to merge.

theme_a.name: Grid Modernization & Transmission Equipment
theme_a.description: Transformer, switchgear, and grid-equipment makers with multi-year backlogs driven by surging datacenter and electrification-driven grid interconnect demand.

theme_b.name: AI Data Center Power Infrastructure
theme_b.description: Power-generation, grid-interconnect, and cooling names re-rating on hyperscaler datacenter electricity demand.

pairs.rationale: The mirror of M09: DIFFERENT names/sector labels, SAME driver (datacenter electricity demand hitting the grid). A driver-based adjudicator merges (or nests) these; a label-based one wrongly keeps them apart. Tests the merge direction, not just the distinct direction.

theme_a.name: GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drug Makers
theme_a.description: Developers and manufacturers of GLP-1 agonist obesity/diabetes drugs riding the metabolic-drug demand supercycle.

theme_b.name: GLP-1 Collateral-Damage Consumer Staples
theme_b.description: Snack, confectionery, and beverage names UNDER PRESSURE from feared GLP-1-driven consumption decline - the theme tracks the same story from the short side.

pairs.rationale: The same-narrative/opposite-exposure trap: one story, OPPOSITE trade direction and member economics. Merging a long-beneficiary theme with its collateral-damage complement would blend inverse exposures - thesis coherence requires the same DIRECTIONAL driver, not the same headline.

theme_a.name: Cybersecurity Platform Consolidators
theme_a.description: Broad-platform security vendors gaining share as enterprises consolidate point products onto platforms.

theme_b.name: Zero-Trust Network Edge Security
theme_b.description: Zero-trust and SASE edge-security specialists benefiting from the same enterprise security-spend cycle, as a specific architecture slice.

pairs.rationale: Textbook parent-child: the zero-trust slice rides the same enterprise security-spend driver as a narrower architecture story. MERGE is wrong (the slice has distinct members/economics); the tested error is merging.

theme_a.name: Uranium Miners & Converters
theme_a.description: Uranium producers and conversion-capacity names driven by the uranium price cycle and utility contracting.

theme_b.name: Small Modular Reactor Developers
theme_b.description: SMR design and deployment names driven by datacenter-linked nuclear power-purchase announcements and licensing milestones.

pairs.rationale: Both 'nuclear', different drivers and cycles: commodity price/contracting vs deployment-milestone speculation. A nuclear-stem merge is the label error; DISTINCT is golden (a nuclear-renaissance PARENT_CHILD nesting is defensible, MERGE is not).

theme_a.name: Bitcoin Mining & Crypto Infrastructure Operators
theme_a.description: Bitcoin miners and crypto-infrastructure operators leveraged to the BTC price cycle and hashprice economics.

theme_b.name: Bitcoin Miners Pivoting to AI Compute
theme_b.description: Former pure-play miners re-rating on conversion of their power/datacenter footprints into AI-compute hosting contracts - the driver is the AI-compute conversion, not the BTC cycle.

pairs.rationale: The membership-overlap trap: HEAVY ticker overlap (the same companies), but the theses are different drivers (BTC price vs AI-conversion re-rating) with different catalysts and different winners within the cohort. Shared tickers must not force a merge when the DRIVERS diverge - the inverse of M10.
